coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 5–6 miles, Z2 only (130–140 bpm max), mostly flat or rolling. Your last three runs show consistent Z2 work at 128–132 bpm, which is exactly right for taper—you're maintaining aerobic capacity without accumulating fatigue 4 days out. Today is a shakeout to flush legs and keep the engine ticking. Stop at 6 miles if you feel heavy; this is not a confidence builder, it's a momentum keeper. Aim for 45–50 min total, zero intensity.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Eat to your travel schedule, not your training. You've likely logged corporate time already this week—prioritize 3–4 solid meals with carbs + protein rather than fueling around a token easy run. Aim for 150g carbs and 25–30g protein per meal to top off glycogen without overloading your gut 96 hours before a 50K. If you're flying or driving to Slovenia today or tomorrow, hydrate aggressively and avoid high-fiber foods 48 hours before race day.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your RHR is 56 (down 8.7 bpm from 30-day avg), sleep is 8.3h at 88.8% efficiency, and recovery score is 92/100—you are objectively ready. Maintain that 8+ hours through race week; don't break the sleep habit now. No massage guns, no ice baths, no extra stretching that taxes the nervous system. Sleep is your only recovery modality this week. If you're traveling today, prioritize sleep over training volume—a 5-hour flight + 2 hours of driving trumps a 6-miler.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're 4 days out with a fully recovered system and a tapered training week. The work is done; Julian Alps 50K's 2,500m of vert and sparse aid stations are now a test of pacing discipline and mental toughness, not fitness. Use these next 96 hours to visualize the climb profiles, review aid station locations, and dial in your race fueling plan. Trust the taper. Easy runs feel sluggish right now—that's normal and necessary. You don't prove anything in week 22.
